comparator.name: Spanish Language and Culture
comparator.route: Transatlantic Perspectives on Spain and Latin America
comparator.sourceNotes: The standard Spanish track includes a 127.5 EC major and 52.5 EC of electives. This example follows the published rotation for students starting in 2026. It includes a Spanish-language thesis and keeps the 30 EC elective package and 22.5 EC of other electives open.
components: First course in the Spanish language sequence, working toward CEFR A1.
Introduces methods for interpreting literary texts.
Second course in the Spanish language sequence, working toward CEFR A2.
Compares how languages form words and sentences.
Third course in the Spanish language sequence, working toward CEFR B1.
Teatro, cine e intermedialidad: España y América Latina
Studies theater and cinema in Spain and Latin America and how they interact with other media.
Fourth course in the Spanish language sequence, working toward CEFR B2.
Studies Spanish in its social contexts in Spain and Latin America.
Competencias de lectura y conciencia cultural: España y América Latina
Develops reading skills and cultural awareness through material from Spain and Latin America.
Studies migration and diaspora in the Transatlantic Perspectives package.
Testimonios, crónicas, representaciones: España y América Latina
Studies testimonies, chronicles and representation in Spain and Latin America.
Examines how language varies and changes.
An approved research methods choice focused on intercultural communication.
Electives beyond the 30 EC package, subject to Utrecht’s degree rules.
Lengua, cultura e identidad: España y América Latina
One of two additional advanced courses. It examines language, culture and identity in Spain and Latin America.
One of two additional advanced courses. It examines contested interpretations of the past.

routeSelection.route: Transatlantic Perspectives on Spain and Latin America
routeSelection.basis: The standard track represents the broad degree through study of Spanish and of Spain and Latin America. The 2026 intake is scheduled for the four odd-year courses in year two. The two first listed even-year courses meet the additional depth requirement in year three. Research Methods Intercultural Communication is an approved choice that supports the track’s study of migration and cultural identity. Crossing Borders is a separate eligible track.

core: Spanish proficiency, grammar, variation and Spanish linguistics
Spanish and Latin American literature, literary interpretation, theatre, film and text-based research
Histories and cultures of Spain and Latin America, transatlantic relations, colonial legacies, migration and cultural memory
adjacent: Language, identity, society, intercultural communication and cultural expression across languages

courses: New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory
trace: uses historical sources to study modernity, nationalism, migration, imperialism, dictatorship and decolonization
introduces sociological theory in its imperial and colonial context and explicitly examines the exclusion of race and gender from canonical accounts
establishes practical criticism, genre analysis and film-narrative basics for close study of literary texts
studies film history, form and political context as an evolving cultural expression
builds reflective and collaborative skills through personal and professional development in the shared UCR core
traces how trade, colonization and contact with Islamic courts, Africa, Asia and the Americas shaped Renaissance Italian art
compares major works and literary forms through questions of memory, agency, colonialism and narrative power
uses stylistics and literary linguistics to analyse how phonetic, grammatical and discoursal choices create meaning in texts
studies empires, power and competing explanations of imperial rise and decline, directly supporting the evidenced colonial-legacy direction
compares myth and storytelling across cultures and media through questions of power, gender and narrative agency
analyses how material media shape communication, knowledge circulation and cultural memory
studies European institutions, public authority, interests and legitimacy as contemporary political context for Spain within Europe
examines West African visual cultures, colonial collecting, diaspora reinterpretation and repatriation as concrete colonial and postcolonial cultural history
uses Indigenous storytelling, primary sources and oral history to investigate colonial violence, resistance and Indigenous resurgence in North America
develops qualitative interviewing and interpretation of situated social meanings for research on communities, identity and intercultural experience
analyses memoir, autobiography, diary and travel narratives as culturally situated accounts of identity and encounter
uses social theory and civil society case research to examine public spheres, migrant solidarity and decolonial critique
connects modern art including Mexican muralism with questions of curating, reception and Eurocentrism
develops methods for analysing literary-to-film adaptation, narration, image, music and sound as cultural expression
studies how film, photography and music reproduce or resist racial power and how cultural expression records oppression and resistance
guides students from historical question design and critical source analysis to a substantial research paper
examines the history and methodologies of writing art history, providing advanced cultural interpretation and research writing
applies humanist, feminist, Marxist, minority and psychoanalytic perspectives in an advanced text-research project
analyses documentary representation across historical, social, ethical and aesthetic contexts and includes multimodal production
analyzes rhetorical texts, builds arguments and develops persuasive speeches through writing, debate and oral delivery
uses primary sources, oral history and cultural representations to examine gender, sexuality and intersecting identities
uses community-based coaching, storytelling and debate to build public speaking skills with local schoolchildren
examines identity, marginalisation and social change through twentieth- and twenty-first-century popular media narratives
examines ethical persuasion and message framing through sustainability communication and a practical science communication project
studies poetry, performance, voice, sound and historically situated formal experimentation through critical and creative work
uses film, image and sound analysis to examine environmental narratives, including Indigenous and postcolonial media

alternatives.label: Literature, empire and cultural memory
alternatives.concept: Explore how empires, migration and resistance shape stories, art and public memory. Compare literature and film, trace colonial exchange through art and history, and design a historical research project.
alternatives.labelReason: The title reflects the central subjects and methods of the selected courses.
progression: Introductions to literature, history and film lead into comparative literature, empire and heritage. Qualitative methods and historical interpretation prepare students for advanced cultural analysis and independent historical research.

alternatives.label: Literature, rhetoric and media
alternatives.concept: Explore how literature, public speaking and media shape identity and public debate. Study stories across media, coach public speaking in a community setting and design persuasive messages on environmental issues.
alternatives.labelReason: The title reflects the central subjects and methods of the selected courses.
progression: Introductory rhetoric precedes community speaking and advanced persuasion. Literary and film foundations lead into adaptation, documentary and creative communication.
alternatives.distinctness: Seven courses and 52.5 EC differ in each direction. The first option focuses on empire, colonial history, museums and historical research. The second focuses on public speaking, persuasion, creative communication, gender history and contemporary media.

candidates.label: Language, identity and cultural expression across media

selection.assessment: Two plans support related cultural and literary interests. The active UCR course evidence does not support a third coherent plan centered on Spanish acquisition, Spanish linguistics and writing. General stylistics and rhetoric courses support the related directions.

blocks: Utrecht’s sequence develops Spanish proficiency through CEFR A1 at this stage.
Utrecht’s sequence develops Spanish proficiency through CEFR A2 at this stage.
Utrecht’s sequence develops Spanish proficiency through CEFR B1 at this stage.
Utrecht’s sequence develops Spanish proficiency through CEFR B2 at this stage.
Utrecht compares how languages structure words and sentences. UCR’s stylistics course examines how choices in language create effects in texts.
Utrecht studies Spanish in its social contexts in Spain and Latin America.
Utrecht studies language variation and change as a dedicated subject.
Utrecht examines the relationship between language and identity in Spain and Latin America.
Utrecht’s Spanish-language writing workshop prepares students for their thesis.
Both introduce methods for interpreting literary texts. UCR’s course surveys literature across traditions.
Both examine how stories move between media. UCR focuses on literature and film adaptation, while Utrecht also studies theater from Spain and Latin America.
Utrecht connects reading skills and cultural awareness with the Spanish-speaking world.
Utrecht focuses on testimony, chronicles and representation from Spain and Latin America. UCR’s life writing course spans a wider range of settings.
Both consider contested readings of history. UCR studies Indigenous North American histories, colonial violence and resistance.
Utrecht includes dedicated study of migration and diaspora. Migrant solidarity is one topic within UCR’s broader social theory course.
Utrecht’s methods course focuses on intercultural communication. UCR teaches qualitative research methods for a wider range of social questions.
Students choose these electives under Utrecht’s degree rules.
Utrecht requires a 7.5 EC thesis written in Spanish. The optional UCR research element sits outside the 180 EC schedule.
Students can complete a minor or another approved package such as study abroad.

notes.text: Both UCR options offer related study in literature, culture and communication. Utrecht adds a sequence in Spanish language, linguistics and writing and sustained study of Spain and Latin America.

audience.programmeDescription: Learn Spanish and study the literature, history and cultures of Spain and Latin America. Utrecht teaches mainly in Spanish, with some courses in English.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The Utrecht example follows the Transatlantic Perspectives track. The UCR options focus on literature and cultural memory or on literature, rhetoric and media.
